html:
The leader of the People's Republic of China from 1978 until about 1989, though he never held the top titles. His market reforms opened China to the world and began its rise to economic power.

Born in Sichuan, he went to France as a young worker-student and joined the Communists there. He took part in the Long March and the civil war and rose high after 1949. In the Cultural Revolution he was purged, came back, and was purged again in 1976.

After Mao Zedong died he outmanoeuvred Mao's chosen heir and in 1978 launched reform and opening:

  • farm families could farm their own plots and sell their surplus, the household responsibility system;
  • the Shenzhen economic zone and others welcomed foreign investment;
  • Hong Kong's return was agreed under "one country, two systems".

He also kept the party's grip. In 1989 he backed the use of the army against the Tiananmen Square protests. His southern tour of 1992 restarted reform. He died months before Hong Kong's handover in 1997.
